headline: Golfer Tom Kim Wins Asian Games Gold, Secures Military Exemption
meta_description: South Korean golfer Tom Kim wins Asian Games gold at Kasugai Country Club, securing exemption from mandatory military service.
summary_short: Tom Kim claimed victory at the Asian Games with a brilliant final round, earning a prized exemption from South Korea's mandatory military service.
body:
Tom Kim, 24, won gold at the Asian Games in Kasugai, Japan, finishing 18 under par and claiming victory by three strokes—a result that frees him from South Korea's mandatory military service requirement. Able-bodied South Korean males must typically serve between 18 and 21 months before turning 28, but the government rewards Asian Games champions and Olympic medallists with an exemption that reduces the obligation to basic training lasting less than a month. Kim's 64 in the final round secured his place among an elite group of athletes, including former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who have used athletic achievement to sidestep years of service.

The stakes made Kim's performance all the more remarkable. He had rushed from the Presidents Cup in the United States to reach Japan, managing on just six hours of sleep and adjusting to a 14-hour time difference. Despite showing signs of nerves with a bogey on the 17th, his five earlier birdies and an eagle gave him the cushion to finish strong, tapping in par on the final hole. The world number 32 visibly released the tension as his ball found the cup.

Kim's victory caps a strong stretch for the golfer, who has won four PGA Tour titles and triumphed at the Scottish Open in July. The exemption means he can now continue building his professional career with minimal disruption—something he had narrowly missed at the Paris Olympics earlier this year, when he finished eighth after tying for third on day one. His countryman SH Kim, 28, was not as fortunate; South Korea's silver in the team event did not qualify for the exemption.

Finished 18 under par, won by three strokes
Exempts him from 18-21 months of mandatory military service
Rushed from US Presidents Cup on six hours of sleep
World number 32 with four PGA Tour titles
